items.bodyText: David Jaworski, Lauren Greenwood, & Jane Puszkar: Stop Turning Teachers into Therapists – Let Them Teach! Watch this clip from ‘Meet the Candidates Episode 1’ where we tackle the overload on our educators from non-academic mandates: In the clip, David Jaworski calls it out: Teachers are expected to become psychologists for our students, pulling them away from actual teaching. Lauren Greenwood chimes in with a spot-on joke: “(Or their parents!)” – highlighting how these roles blur lines and overstep into family responsibilities. And Jane Puszkar sums it up perfectly: “Let the teachers teach and let the kids be kids!” Programs like these waste valuable time, frustrate our dedicated staff, and distract from core learning. We need to refocus on academics, support teachers in their true expertise, and keep emotional guidance where it belongs—at home or with proper professionals. See the clip: https://youtube.com/.../Ugkx9blMlQtIB1KqQsfqx98nQ9OUEjnGI... Vote April 7, 2026, for a brighter future! #FrancisHowellStrong #letteachersteach #letkidsbekids #VoteDavidJaworski #VoteLaurenGreenwood #VoteJanePuszkar #April7th2026 See less

items.bodyText: What brought us to run for school board? Jane Puszkar: Building a Life of Achievement! Watch this clip from ‘Meet the Candidates Episode 1’ where Jane shares her personal story of resilience and growth: In the clip, Jane reflects on her roots: Born and raised in North St. Louis County as the only girl among three brothers, I learned early on to fight to survive—building the grit and determination that shaped who I am today. I found my perfect husband, started a family with two wonderful children, and then pursued my passions: Earning a degree in accounting, going back for my MBA, and later adding degrees in nursing. Along the way, I built a diverse career, working for Boeing and in pharmaceutical sales, experiences that taught me the value of hard work, innovation, and real-world problem-solving. This background drives my commitment to education—ensuring every child in Francis Howell gets the tools to thrive, just as I fought for my own opportunities. No more distractions; let’s focus on strong, practical learning that prepares kids for real life. See Clip (Part 1) here: https://youtube.com/.../Ugkx-btOs0HCVeD8jg4HlFQJcOdf6Y... (Part 2): https://youtube.com/.../Ugkx... Let’s empower our community together. #FrancisHowell #VoteJanePuszkar #VoteLaurenGreenwood #VoteDavidJaworski #April7th2026 See less

items.bodyText: David Jaworski: Questioning the “Leader in Me” Program and Its Impact on Our Teachers! Watch this clip from ‘Meet the Candidates Episode 1’ where I address the issues with social emotional learning initiatives like the “Leader in Me” program in our district: In the clip, I highlight how programs like “Leader in Me”—meant to teach leadership and emotional skills—are overburdening our educators. Teachers have shared with me that they didn’t sign up for this; they’re being forced to act as psychologists, spending precious classroom time on SEL activities instead of focusing on core academics like reading, math, and science—the jobs they were actually hired to do. This isn’t empowering kids; it’s wasting instructional time and frustrating dedicated teachers who want to teach, not therapize. We need to reevaluate these programs to ensure they’re truly beneficial and not just trendy distractions that pull resources away from real learning. See the clip: https://youtube.com/.../UgkxYXZwafrIZFnRsitSXJaG4xoec1dnT... As a dad who’s seen the fallout firsthand, I’m running with Lauren Greenwood and Jane Puszkar to refocus our schools on proven education, support our teachers, and eliminate wasteful mandates. Vote April 7, 2026, for a board that listens and acts! #FrancisHowellStrong #ParentalRights #VoteDavidJaworski #VoteLaurenGreenwood #VoteJanePuszkar #April7th2026 See less

items.bodyText: Meet the Candidates Episode 1’ Lauren Greenwood and Jane Puszkar share their take on Educational programs & Research based curriculum: In the clip, I urge us to push the pause button on automatically expanding programs across the district. Before we add more, let’s honestly ask ourselves: • What specific problems are we actually trying to solve? • Is what we’re teaching truly valuable and delivering real results for our students? We can’t just keep growing the system without scrutiny. It’s time for thoughtful reevaluation—ensuring every program is necessary, effective, and focused on core academics that prepare our kids for success, while respecting taxpayer dollars and parental priorities. Jane Puszkar also highlights the importance of research-based curriculum—and she’s right. We should strongly encourage (and equip) our educators to use proven, evidence-backed methods that drive measurable learning gains, close achievement gaps, and move away from untested trends. Together we’ll fight for strong, data-driven education that works. See the clip: https://youtube.com/.../UgkxR3jccUr1SZCB98Y2Im6aXzxktq8Fh... items.bodyText: Taxpayers, the Missouri State Auditor’s report on the Francis Howell School District’s superintendent hiring debacle with Dr. Mike Dominguez exposes wasted money and weak leadership. The district paid a search firm over $40,000 — yet we’ve never been refunded despite the $229k+ payout to a superintendent who never started. Some have said Board President Steven Blair was tasked with pursuing that refund. He allegedly heard “no,” tucked his tail, and backed down. Why does Steven Blair run to the lawyers for every move? Our legal expenses have more than doubled since FY 2022: • 2022: $96,627 • 2023: $107,880 • 2024: $134,130 • 2025: $216,980 • 2026: $144,116 YTD At this rate, 2026 could be our highest year yet — all on your tax dollars. Action step: Email Board President Steven Blair at steven.blair@fhsdschools.org and ask him why he didn’t fight harder for your tax dollars and why legal fees keep skyrocketing. Is this the passive leadership we want protecting our wallets? Real accountability means demanding better — not rolling over. Parents deserve board members who fight for fiscal responsibility. What do you think? #FHSD #TaxpayerAccountability #stevenblair #carolieowens #FHSD See less

items.bodyText: David Jaworski: The Flaws in ‘No Child Left Behind’ – Prioritizing Tests Over True Education! Watch this clip from ‘Meet the Candidates Episode 1’ where David breaks down the rise of the “No Child Left Behind” era and its lasting effects on our schools: In the clip, David discusses how “No Child Left Behind” shifted focus from genuine learning to constant repetition and memorization—just drilling facts to pass tests. That’s not real teaching; it’s a system designed so schools could chase high scores and secure funding, often at the expense of critical thinking, creativity, and well-rounded education. Lauren Greenwood jumps in with the perfect question: “Why are we doing this?” – challenging us to rethink priorities that put bureaucracy over kids. We need to move beyond test-driven mandates and back to empowering teachers with tools for meaningful instruction that prepares students for life, not just exams. See the clip: https://youtube.com/.../UgkxuM1sF2wkQ7... Let’s teach kids to think, not just test. #FrancisHowell #NoChildLeftBehind #VoteDavidJaworski #VoteLaurenGreenwood #VoteJanePuszkar #April7th2026 See less

items.bodyText: TRANSPARENCY ISN’T HARASSMENT. PARENTAL INVOLVEMENT ISN’T EXTREMISM. If you classify bringing the TRUTH about what’s actually happening in your child’s classroom as “harassment,” then you’ve got a serious misconception about what harassment actually is. Sharing proof, of what’s being recommended or provided isn’t bullying — it’s called being an involved parent. It’s called transparency. It’s called PROTECTING KIDS and YOUR PARENTAL RIGHTS. Real harassment is trying to silence parents who dare to look inside the classroom and speak up about what they find. Real harassment is treating moms and dads like enemies for simply letting other parents know what their children are being taught and influenced. If we can’t agree on that basic principle, we’ve lost our way. What do you think — is speaking truth in your child’s education protected, or is it being twisted into something it’s not? items.bodyText: STEVEN BLAIR’S BOARD MEETING REMARKS UNDER SCRUTINY Violation of Francis Howell School District policy during an official public board meeting — or just another “green thing”? Either way, it doesn’t sit right. During a public, taxpayer-funded board meeting, School Board President Steven Blair told the public how we should vote on Senate Bill 3, urging opposition so the district can continue overspending. FHSD policy and Missouri law are clear: District platforms may explain the impact of legislation — but they may NOT advocate for or against a ballot measure. Explaining legislation = appropriate Telling taxpayers how to vote = not appropriate Listen for yourself: https://www.youtube.com/live/5JDMgoCLcic... It appears the district intends to charge ahead with reckless spending, including: • $78,000,000 over budget on the new high school • $230,000 paid to a superintendent who never started • …and plenty more under review More ongoing spending projects are now under scrutiny — stay tuned. I’m voting YES on Senate Bill 3 this April. Anyone else keeping tabs? See less

items.bodyText: Lauren Greenwood: Unlocking Student Potential Through Diverse Learning Styles! Watch this clip from ‘Meet the Candidates Episode 1’ where I share my educational background and why we need to embrace different ways kids learn: In the clip, I talk about my own journey: As a visual learner myself, I’ve seen firsthand how one-size-fits-all teaching falls short. There are many different ways to learn—visual, auditory, kinesthetic, and more—that work better for some students than others. We should consider these methods, identify what their strengths are (like how visuals help with retention and creativity, or hands-on activities build problem-solving skills), and tailor education to play to those strengths. It’s about recognizing individual needs to make learning more effective and engaging, not forcing everyone into the same mold. David Jaworski ties it in perfectly: Being married to a teacher whose thesis focused on “multiple intelligences,” he’s seen the power of this approach up close—acknowledging strengths in areas like linguistic, logical, spatial, or interpersonal intelligence to help every child thrive. See the clip: https://youtube.com/.../UgkxgxY1... Let’s celebrate strengths and set our kids up for success. #FrancisHowell #multipleintelligences #DiverseLearners #VoteLaurenGreenwood #VoteDavidJaworski #VoteJanePuszkar #April7th2026 See less

items.bodyText: Part 2: Continuing from my last post… David Jaworski: Why I’m Running for Francis Howell School Board! Watch this clip from ‘Meet the Candidates Episode 1’ where I share my story: As a dad fighting for our kids’ education, I’ve seen how one-sided propaganda sneaks into our schools—especially through books pushed by librarians directly at vulnerable students. These aren’t random picks; they’re targeted at children on IEPs and individual assistance plans, who deserve real academic support, not divisive ideologies disguised as “inclusive” reading. My daughter’s experience with unbalanced, politically charged materials was eye-opening, but hearing from other families about this targeting makes me wonder: What else are they doing behind closed doors without parental oversight? We need transparency now—to review what’s being recommended, ensure neutrality, and protect all students from hidden agendas. That’s why I’m running for Francis Howell School Board: To prioritize facts over fiction, empower parents, and keep our focus on excellence. See the clip: https://youtube.com/.../UgkxCRv8j1ytMXbVQZSI8N8AtYjvkDlVK... Support David on April 7, 2026! #FrancisHowell #SchoolBoardElection #VoteDavidJaworski #ProtectOurKids #FHSD2026 See less

items.bodyText: Lauren Greenwood & David Jaworski: Supporting Our Teachers by Letting Them Teach! Watch this clip from ‘Meet the Candidates Episode 1’ where we discuss the overburdening of educators in our district: In the clip, I (Lauren Greenwood) point out: I don’t think teachers are even allowed to just teach the basics anymore—they’re demanded to do so much more, stretching them thin across roles they’re not specialized for. There are certain skill sets for a reason; our educators should focus on what they do best: teaching core academics. David Jaworski adds: Teachers aren’t trained to be mental health professionals. It’s not a good use of our teachers’ time or our students’ time to force them into these roles. Some of these things—like emotional and social guidance—are the parents’ responsibility and need to be cared for in appropriate settings, like at home or outside of school, not crowding out classroom learning. See the clip: https://youtube.com/.../Ugkx9blMlQtIB1KqQsfqx98nQ9OUEjnGI... Vote April 7, 2026, for a board that values real education! items.bodyText: SCHOOL FUNDING REALITY CHECK: STOP THE ENDLESS MONEY REQUESTS - THE DATA DOESN’T LIE — WHY IS IT NEVER ENOUGH? Hey School Board — what’s your story this time? Blaming the state doesn’t work when the data shows revenue is UP $7.1M this year and $17M over five years. Try again. At last night’s FHSD Board meeting, Carl Suri (the man in the orange shirt) delivered one of the clearest, most data-driven explanations I’ve heard about school funding. He didn’t get emotional. He just walked through the actual numbers: • District revenue is now $245 million — up $7.1 million this year alone • That increase came entirely from the state (up 10.75%) • Over the last five years, state revenue is up $17 million — a 32% increase • Per-student state funding is at an all-time high, even after inflation His point was simple and hard to argue with: the money keeps going up, yet the district still acts like it’s never enough. He questioned why we keep hearing calls for more local taxes or fund transfers when the data shows revenue has been rising steadily. If you’ve ever felt like “just a little more money” is a permanent answer instead of a temporary one, watch this segment. It’s calm, factual, and cuts through the usual talking points. Link starts right at his comments: https://www.youtube.com/live/SwzYuBTzlnQ?t=218 Watch it. Share it. The numbers matter. See less

items.bodyText: TEACHER CLAIMS VICTIMHOOD AFTER YEARS OF PUBLIC TRANSGENDER ADVOCACY — BUT WHAT ABOUT THE KIDS? Independence Elementary Kindergarten Teacher Becky Hormuth (~20:24) spoke as a victim of supposed bullying and defamation, asking the board for more staff protections. Questions that need answers: • Why is it that when the truth is shared about policies affecting children, staff get to become the victim — while innocent children (including kindergarteners!) are expected to quietly accept changes to bathrooms, social transitions, or gender ideology without their parents’ full knowledge and consent? • Is it not true your own child has transitioned? • Was there not news media coverage in which you voluntarily participated? • Did you not stand up at multiple public school board meetings advocating against sex-based policies for district facilities? • Was the child who came home asking why they’d want to be a boy not connected to your classroom? Parents aren’t harassers for asking hard questions and protecting their kids. The double standard is clear: data and parental rights matter. Watch the full meeting and decide for yourselves. items.bodyText: What brought us to Run for school board? Watch this clip from ‘Meet the Candidates Episode 1’ where David Jaworski opens up about his upbringing and what drives his commitment to our schools: In the clip, David shares his story: Raised right here in St. Louis, with a family history deeply rooted in education and discovery. I pursued a path in the fine arts, but grew up in a household where learning was everything—my mother was a botanist, my father a molecular biologist, and our home was a hub for brilliant minds, including Nobel laureates who came and went, inspiring curiosity and excellence. To top it off, I married a teacher, which has given me even more insight into the daily challenges and triumphs in our classrooms. This background fuels my passion for strong, balanced education that prepares kids for real success. See the clip: https://youtube.com/.../UgkxhoDIk9hxMNFmktibN8pOJfTkof9ro... Let’s honor our roots and build a brighter tomorrow. #FrancisHowell #EducationalExcellence #VoteDavidJaworski #VoteLaurenGreenwood #VoteJanePuszkar #April7th2026 #FHSD See less

items.bodyText: Link to the full book challenge list below! I’m deeply concerned about inappropriate books in our school libraries. I proposed a compromise: move them to an opt-in section for parents who want access, sparing others from challenging titles one by one. items.bodyText: PARENTS THE LONGER YOU WAIT and you don't hold your child's schools accountable gives these guys more time to dictate what's best for your child's physical mental and emotional health. Don’t be afraid to speak out for your kids because they are voiceless and rely on you. Parents — Know Your Rights You do not have to accept every lesson, survey, or program the school offers. Here’s what you can do: Opt out of any content that does not align with your family’s values or beliefs. You have the right to review materials and formally opt your child out. Opt out of surveys and questionnaires. Many are designed to collect personal information about your child’s beliefs, mental health, family life, or identity. You can refuse participation. Request to preview all surveys, social-emotional lessons, and sensitive materials before they are given to your child. Put everything in writing. Send a clear opt-out notice and keep a copy for your records. Stay informed and connected. Talk with other parents, attend school board meetings, and share information. Your child’s education and values start at home. You have the right — and the responsibility — to protect both. See less

items.bodyText: The U.S. Department of Justice and the U.S. Department of Education announced they will pursue enforcement action against Kansas City, Kansas Public Schools, alleging the district violated federal parental-rights and student-privacy laws by shielding students' transgender status from parents. Federal investigators pointed to a district policy stating that school staff "should not disclose information that may reveal a student's transgender status or gender nonconforming presentation to others, including parents." The Education Department's Student Privacy Policy Office opened its investigation in August 2025; in April 2026, it found the district's policy violated the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act, and in June it issued a formal Letter of Impending Enforcement Action after also finding a Title IX violation. Read more in the comments.... See less

items.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Normalize keeping your children away from children who are too exposed Normalize keeping your kids away from children who are too exposed. In today’s world, there are kids with full access to the internet, social media, mature shows, and things their little minds shouldn’t have to process yet. And honestly… it shows. My boys are 6, 5, and 3, and sometimes my husband and I wonder if we’re sheltering them. But the truth is, we’re protecting their innocence. We don’t want them learning things that are far too heavy and too mature for their developing brains. Normalize saying no. Normalize not letting your young children be alone with other children, even “good kids,” simply because you don’t know what those kids have seen, heard, or experienced. This isn’t about judgment, it’s about safety. I was a child who was exposed to way too much, way too young. And I can say, it stays with you. It shapes you. It affects you in ways you don’t even recognize until much later. So if you’re the parent who chooses to limit access, supervise closely, set boundaries, and protect your child’s childhood..you’re not overreacting. You’re not controlling. You’re being a present, aware, loving parent. Protecting their innocence isn’t sheltering. It’s parenting. | n51evETkPd.com

items.author: School Watchlist
items.bodyText: All this outrage about schools, fire, libraries, and disability programs losing funding seems to show up only when taxpayers ask questions and say no more taxes we are tapped out. •Where is that same outrage when developers receive tax abatements and incentives that divert revenue away from our same districts? • St. Charles County’s 2024 incentive report confirms Chapter 100 and Chapter 353 abatements reduce or redirect tax dollars from schools and other local taxing authorities. • In WSD, the 2023 agreement tied to the Bryan Road/Highway N and Feise/Bryan developments includes abatement of real property taxes, with only a $50,000 annual contribution (2024–2036) instead of full taxation. But we just keep building, thousands of new homes and apartments: The Solstice The Sullivan (LSL) New Town expansion (St Charles) Shady Creek (Hwy N) Autumn Hollows (Hwy N) Creekside at Sommers (45 homes across LHS) Inverness (Bryan & Feise) The Prairie & Prairie Encore (190 apartments) Trailside Farms (Hwy N toward LSL) • Are these developments paying their full share, or are incentives shifting that burden to the community? When local officials approve these deals, they are choosing to reduce or delay full tax collections through abatements and other agreements. • Why do developers get tax breaks, while the families already living here pay the increases every year? Before asking taxpayers for more and more money, there should be accountability, transparency, and better long-term planning. See less

items.author: Greenwood for FHSD School Board
items.bodyText: TAX PAYERS PAID TWICE Forced to spend 3k on outside resources A question I keep getting is whether I believe it was a good use of district funds to hire an outside reviewer to evaluate whether books are age-appropriate. Honestly, it’s a shame we were even put in that position. This should have been handled by our own administration, using the policies already in place. Instead, those policies were treated as subjective — and when policy becomes subjective, it might as well not exist at all. When leadership won’t act with clarity or courage, people who care “Jane Puszkar, FHSD Board of Education” (one of my running mates) about protecting students are forced to look for outside resources. That’s not ideal, but it’s a direct result of inaction. My goal is simple: clear, objective policies that are followed — so taxpayers aren’t paying twice, and parents can trust what’s in our schools. ONCE AGAIN, THE FACTS: The district stated to STL Today that the $3,000 purchase followed administrative approval rules and did not require a written contract. No one was forced, and the purchase was within established authority. Link ref: https://www.stltoday.com/.../article_0053bb80-e341-4e3e... Transparency matters, and questions about process are fair. But it’s troubling that a $3,000 review is drawing more outrage than the 78 MILLION Over Budget Spend, or thr presence of sexually age-inappropriate books in our schools. That feels like a distraction from what many parents actually care about. YOUR VOTE = YOUR MONEY FOLLOW ME FOR MORE TRUTHll See less

items.author: Greenwood for FHSD School Board
items.bodyText: If elected to the school board, one of my top priorities will be protecting our kids from age-inappropriate materials in school libraries. No more turning a blind eye to books that violate our Learning Commons policies and expose children to explicit content they’re not ready for. * this would include any staff member violating policy (i.e. classroom libraries, human sexuality, controversial flags￼ etc.)￼ Here’s what I’ll push for: A clear, zero-tolerance enforcement plan for librarians and staff who repeatedly ignore these guidelines. • First offense: Mandatory retraining on policy compliance and a formal written warning. • Second offense: Temporary suspension without pay, plus a review of their book selection process. • Third offense: Recommendation for termination and potential revocation of library credentials within the district. Our schools should be safe spaces for learning, not indoctrination hubs. Parents deserve transparency, and kids deserve protection. Vote for me this April 7 to put families first! #SchoolBoardElection #ProtectOurKids #FamilyValues See less

items.syntheticKey: Greenwood for FHSD School Board|2 April|THE FACTS (not fear) ABOUT PROP RT Know before you go April 7
items.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | • Districts "WILL" still receive funding but no more • automatic increases without voter approval. What specific student programs are actually being reduced if Prop RT doesn’t pass? "None" because it is all speculation. Where is the data showing total revenue vs. total district spending, or even salary breakdowns? • I highly doubt school districts will eliminate transportation services. They "may" adjust routes or distance parameters, but since transportation is not a federally mandated service for general education students it "MUST" be provided for students with IEP's/504 plans. • Salaries or reductions should start at the top with administration not bus drivers, paras, or teachers many of whom already work second jobs. How about showing the funding from sources other than property tax? How much revenue growth still occurs from new construction and reassessment on home sales? How many of those contracts (current and future builds, Prairie Encore or Trailside Farms) receive abatement deals? None of these items you listed are guaranteed cuts just are potential worst case scenario outcomes based on (district admin) decisions. What proven spending adjustments has the district made before claiming these reduced, decreased or delayed meaures will be necessary? • Let’s be honest many of the repairs didn’t just appear overnight. Some have been needed for years, even decades. The question is, where has the priority been, and why are families always expected to keep covering the extra costs? District audits provide a snapshot, not a full deep dive. There should be stronger checks and balances in place to ensure accountability and transparency. Truth is district spending priorities have included high dollar admin salaries and delayed maintenance for x amount of reasons. • Most recently, WSD Superintendent Bishop discussed redistricting, pay-to-play sports, student program cuts, and transportation changes that sound inevitable. These are considerations, not confirmed actions. Presenting only negative outcomes creates the impression of “vote this way or face the consequences,” rather than allowing for informed decisions. • Families are simply tired of being the default solution every time more money is needed. It’s only fair to expect districts and community groups to make adjustments and work within their budget too. Every dollar matters right now. Families should have the freedom to decide where theirs goes. Vote YES on Prop RT Missouri Vote NO Fire & EMS | rrDXH1.com

items.bodyText: A thought on school policies and parenting: I’ve noticed some non-conservative parents arguing against any firm decisions or rules, claiming “everything is subjective.” But if that’s the case, how do we uphold any standards? Without policies that are actually followed, what kind of school are we left with—one with zero guidelines, no accountability, and chaos reigning supreme? It sounds a lot like anarchy, where nothing gets done and everyone suffers. If subjectivity rules all, who’s deciding what’s best for our kids? —curious to hear your take! #EducationMatters #SchoolPolicies #ParentingThoughts See less

items.author: Greenwood for FHSD School Board is with David Jaworski for FHSB at Spencer Road Branch Library.
items.bodyText: Q&A from the Event Here’s a summary of the key questions I received during my speaking opportunity, along with my responses: Q: Who has the most influence on what our students are taught? A: The teachers, because they are the first tier of direct contact with our students. Q: Do you believe there should be safe spaces created in school? A: No, creating them would further division and separation between students. It doesn’t enforce cohesion and respect at all times, and it creates an unrealistic real-world environment. Q: What endorsements and funding have you received, and how does it influence how you’ll vote? A: I’m endorsed by Francis Howell Families and the St. Charles County Republican Committee. I have a personal conviction to vote for what is right, with no outside influences. These supporters already align with my values. Q: Do you think classes like DEI and CRT should be taught? A: Possibly, if we could agree on the appropriate grade level to make it age-appropriate and on what and how it’s taught. The reality is there will always be concerns about teacher bias leading to conflicts with parents’ rights and views. So, with that said, probably not, because we risk teacher bias as well as infringement on parents’ rights on how they want these topics addressed. Q: What would your 3 priorities be as a school board member? A: 1. Fiscal responsibility: Scrutinizing current building projects and educational programs, pressing pause where it makes sense to ask: Is this necessary, and is it helpful to the students? 2. Enforcing policy: Currently, the board and superintendent do not follow policy and make everything subjective. 3. Being a good example: Doing what’s right even when it’s not always popular, to encourage others who feel suppressed to stand up for what’s right. See less

items.bodyText: THIS IS ACUAL DISCRIMINATION It’s interesting how often people say they’re “not against anybody’s religion,” yet in the same breath argue that anyone with a biblical worldview shouldn’t have a voice in public education. Here’s the problem with that thinking: Public schools are meant to serve everyone — including families who hold religious beliefs. Wanting people of faith excluded from decision-making doesn’t promote neutrality; it promotes one worldview while shutting out another. You don’t have to agree with someone’s beliefs to respect their right to participate. A biblical foundation shapes many people’s morals, ethics, and approach to leadership — the same way others draw from philosophy, culture, or personal life experience. Singling out Christians as uniquely unfit to serve isn’t separation of church and state… it’s discrimination. See less

items.bodyText: Hey Missouri families and educators! Lt. Gov. David Wasinger just launched the “Lieutenant Governor’s Award for American Patriotism” essay contest to celebrate America’s 250th anniversary and inspire patriotism in our kids. Open to all Missouri students in grades K-12. Write a letter using one of these prompts: • “I am proud to be an American because…” • “I love America because…” Word count limits: • Grades K-3: 50 words • Grades 4-6: 100 words • Grades 7-12: 200 words Submission deadline: Entries must be postmarked no later than March 1, 2026. Winners will be honored at a special ceremony and lunch at the Missouri State Capitol on June 26, 2026, where they’ll read their letters aloud! This is a great way for kids to reflect on our nation’s blessings of liberty, faith, family, and freedom. Get those entries in soon—spread the word! For full details: https://ltgov.mo.gov/lieutenant-governor-david-wasinger.../ Project requirements PDF: https://ltgov.mo.gov/.../Letters-to-Lt.-Governor-Project... See less

Finally, special thanks to our wonderful sponsor, Francis Howell Families, for making this event possible. Your energy and enthusiasm fuel this journey—let’s keep pushing forward together! items.bodyText: How Parents Can Check Their Child’s School Library (FHSD) Step 1: Go to the online library https://fhsdschools.follettdestiny.com/portal/portal... • Once on the catalog screen, change Location to “Francis Howell Schools” to search the entire district (Ref: Screenshot 1) ⸻ Step 2: Search • Use Keyword (recommended) • This allows you to search by topics or themes, even if you don’t know a specific title or author ⸻ Step 3: Review results • Look for “Interest Level” (ex: Elementary, Middle, Young Adult) • This can help you question whether the content fits your child’s age (Ref: Screenshot 2) ⸻ Step 4: Click “Details” • Read the summary/description of the book (Ref: Screenshot 3) ⸻ Step 5: Click “Copies” (top right) • See which schools currently have the book (Ref: Screenshot 4) ⸻ How to Challenge a Book • First, contact your child’s building principal • If needed, complete the district’s official review form and submit it as instructed Book Challenge Form https://resources.finalsite.net/.../Review-of-Learning... Ref: Learning Commons Policy 6310 https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/goto?open... Ref: Challenged Policy 6341 https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/goto?open... You can submit the completed form to the superintendent as listed on the document. See less

items.author: Greenwood for FHSD School Board
items.bodyText: Why are middle school students centering their identity on sexuality and politics? In response to non supporters speaking lies about my views, I clarify: I do not teach my children to hate anyone, but to be kind to all—they actively befriend all kids, regardless. Specific example, when they befriended a group that happened to be LGBTQ. After my child’s name introduction, the first response was, “I’m a lesbian.” My child was confused why someone would introduce themselves that way, but still proceeded to be their friend. Over time, they fixated on their sexual preference, hating Trump (unprompted by my child), and probing my kid’s religion. My child responded with grace, but it raises an issue: Why are middle school students centering their identity on sexuality and politics? Schools should promote respect without agendas pushing early self-definition. I’m wary of candidates or anyone administering to our school district favoring affirmation over neutrality for all. I support disciplining bullying—no harassment tolerated. But I oppose elevating groups in ways seen as favoritism or enabling reverse bullying. Let’s unite for great education. Vote wisely on April 7th. See less

Schools should promote respect without agendas pushing early self-definition. I’m wary of candidates or anyone administering to our school district favoring affirmation over neutrality for all. I support disciplining bullying—no harassment tolerated. But I oppose elevating groups in ways seen as favoritism or enabling reverse bullying. Let’s unite for great education. Vote wisely on April 7th. | HtrlD1P1.com

items.bodyText: Following district policy is not harassment. Raising concerns about age-appropriate content is not hate. Disagreeing does not justify abuse. What kind of learning community responds to concerns with intimidation and name-calling? Just a sample of threats and what I’ve been called during this process: • “Most recently, I was labeled a “faux (fake) Christian,” “white,” “heterosexual,” and warned “don’t screw up my kids’ diversity” • “They mess with one of our kids, they mess with all of us” • “Dimwitted” • “bully/intimidate/cause trouble” • “Toxic candidate” • “Book banning is for dummies” • “Anti-intellectual” • “Mouth breather” • “Idiot” • “Racist” • “Illiterate” • “Not competent to read” • “Children shouldn’t suffer for the sins of their parents” • “Stupid” • “People in green/wood houses shouldn't throw stones” • “living in glass houses, mind-bogglingly unaware of their own children's reality” This is deeply concerning, and it needs to be said. I have not attacked or harassed anyone. I have raised documented, firsthand concerns regarding my child’s 7th grade English class at Hollenbeck and both of my children’s school libraries. The irony is clear: this ‘learning community’—including the teacher herself—has exposed her identity far more than I ever did. Attacking my religion in response is inappropriate and reflects clear hypocrisy rather than engagement with the issue. This should concern every parent. Given this, I now question whether I should be the one issuing cease-and-desist letters sighting harassment, misrepresentations, extreme emotional distress, damage to my reputation. Would that take the focus off the kids? Because the focus hasn’t been on kids at all—it’s been on adult agendas/identities. See less

items.bodyText: WAS TRANSGENDER INSTRUCTION GIVEN TO VERY YOUNG STUDENTS WITHOUT PARENT CONSENT? Last night it was reported that a teacher allegedly has violated Board Policy 6116 (Human Sexuality) by discussing transgender-related topics with a very young audience. While board member Sarah Oelke quickly tries to dismiss in attempt to discredit THE TRUTH WILL COME OUT! Listen here: https://youtube.com/.../UgkxKJRO6uYAwk6si4g6v2IwL8hVQLh0B... This policy is explicit and unambiguous: Human sexuality instruction may not occur without prior parent notification and consent. That safeguard exists for a reason — to protect children and to respect parents. So the questions are simple and fair: • What are the ramifications for violating this policy? • How did this happen inside a classroom? • And most importantly — what concrete steps will the district take to ensure this never happens again? Parents should not have to discover policy violations after the fact, through their children. Transparency matters. Policies matter. And when they are broken, accountability must follow. Take Action: Email or call these decision-makers and demand they stop violating policy and protect our children: Chief Academic Officer Glenn Hancock – Glenn.Hancock@fhsdschools.org | (636) 851-4036 Superintendent Mark Delaney – mark.delaney@fhsdschools.org | (636) 851-4000 t See less

items.bodyText: Book Challenge MIDDLE SCHOOL Alert: The Eyes of the Dragon Locations: Francis Howell Middle, Howell High, Howell North Rating: 4 (Mature themes and violence) Contains: • Murder of a queen during childbirth, poisoning and framing a royal heir • Graphic animal cruelty (stoning of a dog) and magical manipulation • Sexual violence (rape implications), sexual content involving minors • Alcohol/drug use, imprisonment, torture, and death of parents Ref links: [pluggedin.com], [supersummary.com], [app.thesto...ygraph.com] Why This Book Violates District Policy District policy prohibits: • Explicit sexual descriptions, including rape or sexual violence (implied sexual assault of a minor) • Materials glamorizing or instructing drug/alcohol use • Violence including murder, torture, animal cruelty, sexual violence, child abuse/kidnapping This book contains these elements, making it in direct conflict with Board‑approved collection standards. Parents: Despite its fantasy veneer and Stephen King’s reputation, The Eyes of the Dragon includes explicit violence, sexual assault implications, and disturbing themes involving minors and animals. Awards or genre don't shield its mature content. Do you think this belongs in our school libraries? Comment below and share this post to raise awareness! Hint: 78 million over budget on new HS, 230k payout to a superintendent that never started TAKE ACTION! Vote YES See less

items.bodyText: Attention Parents of Francis Howell North Students: Just a heads up (in case you missed it in ENews) – Sexual Abuse Prevention presentations from The Child Advocacy Center of Northeast Missouri are scheduled during English classes on the following dates: • February 3 • February 4 • February 5 • February 10 • February 11 • February 12 • April 13 • April 14 • April 15 • April 16 • April 17 I had the chance to review a private preview of the presentation materials beforehand, which informed my perspective. While I fully see the value in programs like this for educating on abuse prevention and empowering teens with knowledge about consent and boundaries, parts of it—like statements emphasizing that “every person has their own personal boundaries and consent,” and discussions that seem to normalize sexual relationships among teens—left me not 100% comfortable. It’s not about dismissing the program’s intent; it’s about highlighting that parents might want a say in how these sensitive topics are introduced, especially if it doesn’t align with their family values. I personally will be allowing my child to participate. For questions, concerns, or to get an opt-out form, please reach out to Dr. Erin Steep at erin.steep@fhsdschools.org or (636) 851-5031. Website: https://www.cacnemo.org/ Keeping you informed! See less

items.bodyText: Francis Howell School District is failing to follow its own policies, putting ideology over rules and student well-being. Here’s the proof: 1. Human Sexuality Policy 6116 and Regulation explicitly state that staff should not make value judgments on sexuality, avoid conversations about it, and direct questions to parents. Yet, teachers are reading books about transgender surgeries to elementary kids and maintaining private “Pride libraries” in classrooms with books on boys having romantic encounters with boys—recommended as reading projects. This directly violates the policy. 2. Learning Commons Policy 6310 is ignored by allowing age-inappropriate books that clearly violate Missouri statutes (like those promoting explicit content) and the district’s own guidelines on educational suitability. 3. In-Classroom Library Policy (under 6310/6341) requires all books to be provided in a list to the board for review and prohibits bringing in books not already in the district library. This isn’t happening—unauthorized books are everywhere, the superintendent knows, and nothing’s being done. 4. Transgender Progress flags are hung in multiple classrooms violating Policy 6242 Religious or Controversial Issues. Parents, demand accountability! Contact the board and superintendent today at Board@fhsdschools.org. #FHSD #SchoolAccountability #ProtectOurKids Policy Links: • Human Sexuality Policy 6116: https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/goto?open... • Human Sexuality Regulation: https://go.boarddocs.com/.../Reg%206116%20-%20Human... • Learning Commons Policy 6310: https://go.boarddocs.com/.../P6310%20-%20Learning... • In-Classroom Library Policy (under 6310/6341): https://go.boarddocs.com/.../P6310%20-%20Learning... • Policy 6242 Religious or Controversial Issues: https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/goto?open... See less

items.bodyText: Some experiences show it might be fostering division among kids: (These are my recent experiences) • At the Rec Plex pool, young black boys (around age 10) said to each other, white swimmers should clear a lane “because it’s Black History Month.” • My daughter’s biracial friend texted a group chat to the white friends “so what you guys gonna be doing for me since it’s black history month”, or it means they don’t care. And “you guys didn’t go through what we had to”. • A new Black student was seen texting “I hate all these white people at this school”. These moments highlight a growing divide—let’s discuss how to teach history in ways that build bridges, not walls. Thoughts? #BlackHistoryMonth #CommunityUnity See less

items.author: School Watchlist
items.bodyText: WALKOUT HAPPENING NOW! Students at Francis Howell North are currently participating in a walkout right now. Reports say at least 50+ kids have left class to protest (details on the exact cause are still unclear—some are speculating it could be related to ICE/immigration enforcement, but it might not be. No official confirmation yet). This is happening DURING school hours, unlike Fort Zumwalt where similar things were organized AFTER school. Will these students be held responsible? Will there be absences marked, detentions, or other consequences like in past walkouts? Or will the district look the other way? Superintendent Mark Delaney hasn’t responded yet with any official statement (as far as I know), but this seems disruptive to the school day. Anyone have more details or eyewitness accounts? #FrancisHowellNorth #FHN #Walkout #StudentProtest See less

items.bodyText: The district has allowed political issues to divide us. Even though I am a Christian, I understand we will never all agree on political issues—that’s why I’m advocating for neutrality in my role. I will not be advocating for Christian flags, the 10 Commandments on the walls, or prayer being enforced in classrooms. However, that also means other controversial symbols and gender ideologies will also not be allowed. In my mind, that is true neutrality. Of course I would prefer things like prayer in the classroom, but I will not force that on anyone, and that is my compromise. However, I will not be advocating for boys being allowed in girls’ facilities (or girl in boy’s facilities). Lines have to be drawn if they are to continue to be moved See less

items.author: School Watchlist
items.bodyText: PRIVATE PRIDE Libraries In Classrooms I recently discovered “private pride libraries” in our 7th grade English class at Hollenbeck Middle School. Some of these books were not found in the library commons, so they appear to be in direct violation of the In-Classroom Library Policy (under 6310/6341). This policy requires all books to be provided in a list to the Board for review and prohibits bringing in books not already in the district library. This isn’t happening — unauthorized books are everywhere, the superintendent knows, and nothing’s being done. This also violates my rights as a parent, as I am unable to monitor or consent to what my child is reading in class. Violation Scenario If a classroom library includes books not reported or approved via the Learning Commons process, the teacher (or district) is in violation: • They bypassed the required transparency steps, since new titles aren’t disclosed to the Board. • They may also be subject to challenges under Policy 6341, which treats classroom and school library materials identically. [go.boarddocs.com] – Please email your concerns to Board@fhsdschools.org #SchoolTransparency #ParentalRights #FHSD #FrancisHowell #AgeAppropriateEducation See less

items.bodyText: WOKE COLLEGES Parents, it’s time we talk openly about where we’re sending our kids for college. Even Webster University—right here in our own backyard—has fully embraced the “woke” agenda. “Diversity is a foundation for a civil society” Dr. Tim Keane, President, Webster University I believe true civil society is built on merit, shared values, free inquiry, and equal opportunity—not identity politics or enforced diversity quotas. We owe it to our children to choose universities that prioritize education over ideology. Do your homework on campus culture, viewpoint diversity, and what students are actually learning. What schools are you considering (or avoiding) for your kids? —our children’s future depends on it. #CollegeChoices #HigherEducation #ParentalResponsibility See less

items.author: School Watchlist is with State Senator Nick Schroer.
items.bodyText: Francis Howell Parents — Momentum is on our side! This week, the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals delivered a major win for parents and taxpayers. The court ruled that authors and publishers do not have a right to force sexually explicit materials into public school libraries. The case involved Iowa’s SF 496, which requires age-appropriate books and removes materials depicting sex acts. The court made it clear: • The First Amendment does not guarantee any book at taxpayer expense. • Removing explicit content is not a “book ban.” Missouri parents, it’s time to act. Age-inappropriate and sexually explicit materials still don’t belong in our kids’ schools — especially in elementary and middle grades. Contact our St. Charles County senators today and urge them to introduce or support strong legislation like Iowa’s SF 496 (and back SB 483 sponsored by Sen. Nick Schroer to protect kids from explicit sexual material): Use the email draft below. The more voices, the stronger the message. Our kids’ innocence and education come first. Share with other FHSD parents! #FrancisHowell #ProtectOurKids #ParentalRights #SB483 ———————————————————————— Email Draft (Copy & Paste Ready) To: adam.schnelting@senate.mo.gov, nick.schroer@senate.mo.gov Subject: Remove Age-Inappropriate Materials from Missouri Schools Dear Senator Schnelting and Senator Schroer, I am a parent in the Francis Howell School District in St. Charles County. I urge you to champion legislation similar to Iowa’s SF 496 and to support SB 483 (sponsored by Sen. Schroer) to strengthen protections against explicit sexual material in schools. Recent rulings, including this week’s Eighth Circuit decision, confirm that schools have the authority and responsibility to keep age-inappropriate books — especially those depicting or describing sex acts — out of classrooms and libraries, particularly for K-6 students. Parents deserve transparency and the right to protect their children’s innocence. Taxpayer-funded schools should focus on education, not exposing kids to explicit content. Please take the lead on this issue in the next legislative session. I would appreciate any update on your plans to protect Missouri families. Thank you for your strong advocacy for St. Charles County families. Sincerely, See less

items.bodyText: Move St. Charles County School Board Elections to November for Higher Turnout￼ Missouri Senate Bill 1002 would move St. Charles County school board elections and tax increase votes to the November general election for much higher voter turnout. Sponsored by Senator Adam Schnelting, the bill has passed the Senate and is now in the House. Why this is a win for parents and taxpayers: • April 7 turnout was only 19% — a tiny fraction of voters decided the entire Francis Howell School Board. • November elections typically see 60-70%+ turnout, giving everyday families a real voice instead of letting special interests dominate. - For example special interests (including teachers’ unions like the MNEA/NEA) are actively organizing to kill the bill so they can keep low-turnout April elections that favor organized special interests. • School board decisions affect our kids and millions in taxes — they deserve broad community input, not low-turnout insider control. • This puts power back where it belongs: with parents and taxpayers. This isn’t partisanship — it’s basic democracy and accountability. =============================== Call or email your Missouri State Representative TODAY and tell them to SUPPORT SB 1002. =============================== Always include your full address to confirm you’re a constituent. • Tricia Byrnes (District 63 – Wentzville area)�Email: Tricia.Byrnes@house.mo.gov�Phone: (573) 751-1460 • Deanna Self (District 64 – parts of O’Fallon, St. Paul, etc.)�Email: Deanna.Self@house.mo.gov�Phone: (573) 751-1484 • Wendy Hausman (District 65 – St. Peters, Cottleville, parts of St. Charles)�Email: Wendy.Hausman@house.mo.gov�Phone: (573) 751-3717 • Scott Miller (District 69 – additional St. Charles County areas overlapping FHSD)�Email: Scott.Miller@house.mo.gov�Phone: (573) 751-5365 • Terri Violet (District 104 – parts of St. Charles County / FHSD)�Email: Terri.Violet@house.mo.gov • Travis Wilson (District 106 – St. Charles area)�Use the contact form on house.mo.gov/MemberDetails.aspx?district=106 (no public direct email listed). • CC - adam.schnelting@senate.mo.gov, nick.schroer@senate.mo.gov See less

items.bodyText: Judge Requires Parental Notification for Elementary School Gender Lessons A book called “My Shadow is PINK” Brave fifth-grader Shea Encinas stood up to his California school after they forced him to read the book My Shadow Is Pink and teach gender identity lessons to a kindergartner—without allowing his family to opt out. Despite their Christian beliefs being ignored, Shea and his parents fought back… and won! The Encinitas Union School District has now dropped its appeal, meaning SCHOOLS MUST GIVE PARENTS ADVANCE NOTICE and the right to OPT their kids OUT of such content. This is a powerful victory for parental rights and religious freedom! Link to article: https://www.californiafamily.org/.../victory-for-parents.../ YouTube interview: https://youtu.be/mdv5LhmLTvg?si=W0cpdH9dSgg0YDqv #ParentalRights #ProtectOurKids #MyShadowIsPink #StandForFaith @firstlibertyinstitute See less

items.bodyText: PARENTS: WAKE UP ON SOCIAL EMOTIONAL LEARNING! Just received this email from the Character Strong program, which is implemented throughout the Francis Howell School District. They’re doubling down next year — pushing Tier 2 small groups and Tier 3 one-on-one interventions for kids’ “MENTAL HEALTH NEEDS.” Social Emotional Learning is now front and center… while academics take a backseat. Real question: If kids need this much emotional intervention at school, isn’t the real problem at HOME? Broken families, no structure, endless screens, checked-out parents? We’re treating symptoms with expensive programs instead of fixing the root. How do we actually solve this where it starts — in the home? Thoughts? Speak up before next year. EMAIL: Board@FHSDSchools.org See less

items.bodyText: WHERE DO YOU DRAW THE LINE? Public schools should educate—not indoctrinate. • Flying sexual flags endorses adult ideologies that contradict the faith of many Christian families. • Stocking libraries with sexual and vulgar books for all ages exposes kids to inappropriate content. • Hiding books in classroom libraries keeps parents in the dark. • Threatening lawsuits to allow boys in girls’ or girls’ in boys locker rooms and restrooms violates privacy, safety, and fairness. The line is simple: Age-appropriate academics, full transparency with parents, and basic biological reality. Schools serve children and families—not activist agendas. Demand curriculum review, parental notification, and neutral education. Your voice matters. See less

items.bodyText: SPORTS FORM: HOW DOES YOUR CHILD IDENTIFY? Did you know that the sports physical forms required for Missouri kids to play school team sports come from MSHSAA (Missouri State High School Activities Association)? These standard forms now include the question: “How does your child identify?” In no way, shape, or form should “identifies as” belong on a sports physical form. It should be sex assigned at birth — period! This is about protecting fair competition and common sense. Contact the MSHSAA Board today and voice your concerns. • Jim Welby (St. Louis) — jwelby@stdominichs.org • email@mshsaa.org Or what’s next… boys competing in girls sports and vice versa? Parents — it’s time to speak up now. See less

items.bodyText: FHSD Parents & Taxpayers: Questions on the New “No Tax Rate Increase” Props O & H Headed to November The Board just voted to put two propositions on the November 3, 2026 ballot that they’re marketing as “no-tax-rate-increase” measures. Here’s the quick breakdown: Proposition O – Levy Transfer Shifts 12.5 cents from the debt service levy to the operating levy. The district says this will add roughly $5.5 million per year to the operating budget (for salaries, buses, food service, etc.) without raising your overall tax rate. They cite a ~$9.3 million state funding shortfall over the next two years plus rising costs for labor, insurance, fuel, and supplies. Proposition H – $150 Million Bond Issue For “critical facility needs” across all 23 schools — roofs, windows, HVAC, mechanical/electrical systems, safety & security, CTE programs, ADA compliance, sidewalks, parking lots, and athletic/performing arts spaces. Also pitched as no tax rate increase. I have some real questions about these: • For Prop O: Is there really a $9M+ state funding shortfall hitting us this hard right now? What’s the actual story behind the funding formula changes? We need the full, transparent picture — not just the headline number. • For Prop H: It’s interesting they don’t say what will happen to our current bond levy rate if this does NOT pass. Would it actually go down once existing obligations are paid off? And did they have to do any maneuvering or creative structuring to get this labeled a true “no tax increase” bond issue? This comes right after our Prop S experience. What started as a $240 million bond ended up adding another $150 million in costs (totaling around $390 million) because it wasn’t planned or executed right the first time. We can’t keep repeating that pattern. Transparency on these big fiscal moves matters. Our kids, our teachers, and our community deserve straight answers and better planning before we head to the polls. See the attached PDF from the recent board meeting update for the details they released. https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/Public# https://www.fhsdschools.org/.../distric.../post/prop-o-and-h What do you think? Do these questions matter to you too? Have you looked at the numbers? Drop your thoughts in the comments — and keep pushing for real accountability. Share this if you believe more FHSD families should see it. #FHSD #FrancisHowell #PropO #PropH #SchoolBond #TaxTransparency #StCharlesCounty See less

Here’s the quick breakdown: Proposition O – Levy Transfer Shifts 12.5 cents from the debt service levy to the operating levy. The district says this will add roughly $5.5 million per year to the operating budget (for salaries, buses, food service, etc.) without raising your overall tax rate. They cite a ~$9.3 million state funding shortfall over the next two years plus rising costs for labor, insurance, fuel, and supplies. Proposition H – $150 Million Bond Issue For “critical facility needs” across all 23 schools — roofs, windows, HVAC, mechanical/electrical systems, safety & security, CTE programs, ADA compliance, sidewalks, parking lots, and athletic/performing arts spaces. Also pitched as no tax rate increase. I have some real questions about these: • For Prop O: Is there really a $9M+ state funding shortfall hitting us this hard right now? What’s the actual story behind the funding formula changes? We need the full, transparent picture — not just the headline number. • For Prop H: It’s interesting they don’t say what will happen to our current bond levy rate if this does NOT pass. Would it actually go down once existing obligations are paid off? And did they have to do any maneuvering or creative structuring to get this labeled a true “no tax increase” bond issue? This comes right after our Prop S experience. What started as a $240 million bond ended up adding another $150 million in costs (totaling around $390 million) because it wasn’t planned or executed right the first time. We can’t keep repeating that pattern. Transparency on these big fiscal moves matters. Our kids, our teachers, and our community deserve straight answers and better planning before we head to the polls. See the attached PDF from the recent board meeting update for the details they released. https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/Public# https://www.fhsdschools.org/.../distric.../post/prop-o-and-h What do you think? Do these questions matter to you too? Have you looked at the numbers? Drop your thoughts in the comments — and keep pushing for real accountability. Share this if you believe more FHSD families should see it. #FHSD #FrancisHowell #PropO #PropH #SchoolBond #TaxTransparency #StCharlesCounty See less

items.author: Greenwood for FHSD School Board is with Annette Sieve for St. Charles County Council District 3.
items.bodyText: BILL EIGEL MEET & GREET What an incredible evening! A huge thank you to Bill Eigel for letting me host his meet and greet at our home. I’m truly grateful for the opportunity to bring people together, hear real conversations, and support someone who’s fighting for St. Charles County Missouri. Eliminating Personal Property Tax Stopping High-Density Apartments Preventing Data Centers And here’s the beautiful, full-circle part that still blows my mind: our 176-year-old house actually belonged to Bill’s wife’s family — the Zerr’s— many generations ago. Small world doesn’t even begin to cover it. History has a wonderful sense of humor! I call it God winks As Bill said… “I do believe we are at a crossroads” See less

items.author: Greenwood for FHSD School Board
items.bodyText: FHSD Board Member Sara Dillard at Pride St. Charles (June 20, 2026) Sara Dillard, elected to the Francis Howell School District Board of Education in April 2026, shared this photo from the Pride St. Charles event. —>> SHE IS PICTURED WEARING HER OFFICIAL FRANCIS HOWELL SCHOOL DISTRICT NAME TAG WHILE ATTENDING <<— the event, which featured prominent rainbow and progress pride flags in the background. As a public school board member, this raises questions about personal advocacy and how it aligns with maintaining viewpoint neutrality in district policies, curriculum, and school environments that SERVE ALL FAMILIES. Wearing her official district name tag creates the appearance that FHSD endorses the event. District policies require viewpoint neutrality — personal views should not be presented as official school positions. This raises serious questions about policy violations and potential grounds for FORMAL REVIEW and DISMISSAL! What are your thoughts on elected officials participating in these events while representing the district? Original post from Sarah’s page: https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1ESFmPmzCD/?mibextid=wwXIfr See less

items.bodyText: FERPA Opt-Out Reminder for FHSD Families Did you know? FERPA allows schools to share certain "directory information" (such as a student's name, grade level, honors, activities, or photos) unless a parent/guardian chooses to opt out. You may want to opt out if you prefer that your student's information and/or photos not be included in school publications, websites, social media, yearbooks, news releases, or other approved communications. FHSD Public Notices & FERPA Opt-Out Information: https://www.fhsdschools.org/public-notices Opt Out Form: https://resources.finalsite.net/.../FERPA-and-Media-Opt... Please review the information carefully to determine what is best for your family. See less

items.bodyText: SCHOOL BOARD ELECTIONS MOVING TO NOVEMBER! Governor Kehoe just signed SB 1002 into law! What it does: • Moves school board elections in St. Charles County districts to the November general election (higher turnout!), • makes terms 4 years, and • requires all tax levies/bond issues to go to voters in November too. • Candidates can list party affiliation. ￼ • Starting November 2028 Why it matters: Ends low-turnout April elections that let insiders win. More parents voting = real accountability on spending, curriculum, and policies. Stronger parent voice! Huge thanks to Sen. Adam Schnelting, Rep. Richard West, Nick Schroer and Gov. Kehoe! Read article: https://governor.mo.gov/.../governor-kehoe-takes-action... Ready to make our voices louder? #SB1002 #FrancisHowell #ParentalRights See less

items.bodyText: DEAR EXHAUSTED TEACHERS Some exhaustion is self imposed. Ask yourself is the exhaustion you’re experiencing a direct result of stepping far outside your professional lane? Your job is to teach core subjects — not to promote or encourage any particular lifestyle, sexual identity, or ideology to other people’s children. Stay in your lane as an educator, respect parental rights, and don’t exhaust yourself. *** This teacher was found to maintain an in-classroom PRIDE library at Hollenbeck. Parents deserve transparency: Will those same books and ideology follow them to their new position at Bryan Middle School? *** PARENTS HAVE THE RIGHT TO KNOW. Email: ryan.johnson@fhsdschools.org Bryan Middle Principal See less

items.bodyText: BOOK ALERT The book: Amazons, Abolitionists, and Activists: A Graphic History of Women’s Fight for Their Rights by Mikki Kendall Library: Francis Howell Central Is marketed as a history of women’s rights. In reality, it is a progressive, intersectional feminist narrative that reframes the entire story through modern identity politics. It uses a classroom framing device to walk readers through history while pushing a clear ideological agenda. This book contains: • Explicit inclusion of LGBTQ rights and gender ideology as core parts of “women’s rights” • Promotion of reproductive rights / abortion as a central women’s issue • Intersectional framing that elevates race and identity politics above classical equality or biblical views of men and women • Criticism of early women’s suffrage leaders (including white feminists) for not being progressive enough on race and other modern causes • A strong call to ongoing leftist-style activism presented as the natural continuation of the fight for rights • Adult political content delivered in an accessible graphic novel format aimed at teens If your child is in Francis Howell Central and checking out graphic histories, this is one worth previewing yourself. Not every book with “women’s rights” in the title is teaching the same values. IMPORTANT FOR PARENTS: If you do NOT want your child to have access to this type of content at school, you must contact your school's media specialist (librarian) or your child's principal. Written notification is required. Without it, your child will have full access to any book the school deems appropriate, even material such as this. You can also: • Request a list of books your child has already checked out. • Sign up to receive daily email notifications of every book your child checks out. These options are available at both the elementary and secondary levels. I've said this before, and I'll say it again: we no longer live in an age where adults are protecting children from sexual content. We are living in an age where adults are offering minor children books with age-inappropriate sexual content under the guise of education. I will never stop fighting for our children because every single one of them are worth fighting for! items.bodyText: 1:1 TECHNOLOGY IS COMING TO ALL FHSD MIDDLE & HIGH SCHOOLS Every middle and high school student gets their own take-home Chromebook this fall. Elementary stays with classroom carts. IF IT SOUNDS TOO GOOD TO BE TRUE… IT IS. DO THEY REALLY THINK WE’RE THAT STUPID? The district says this will “save $300,000 a year.” Reality check: • Damage & loss rates jump when devices go home every day (8–12% annually) • Hardware is only ~25% of the real cost — repairs, IT support, and replacements eat the rest • Other districts have spent tens of millions fixing broken Chromebooks that only last 2–3 years • Parents still get hit with repair/replacement fees They also claim “no more screen time.” Giving every middle & high schooler a personal device makes that hard to believe. More screens. Higher long-term costs. This is not a win for students or taxpayers. CONTACT: board@fhsdschools.org See less

items.bodyText: CARL DROPS THE MATH HAMMER ON PROP H Schooling the District on “Free Money” VOTE NO on Prop H The ballot will say $150 million. That’s only the face value of the bonds — not the real cost to taxpayers. We’ve seen this before. Prop S in 2020 said $244 million. The final price tag? $294 million. That’s $50 MILLION MORE than voters approved! How did they do it? They intentionally set higher-than-market interest rates so investors would pay a “premium.” The district got extra cash upfront. Taxpayers get stuck with higher interest payments for the next 10–20 years. The district will try to call that extra $50 million “free money.” There is no such thing as free money. It’s basic time value of money. The mathematics hasn’t changed. They can pick whatever number they want — they just need to be transparent about the true total cost. So far, they’re still refusing to do that. Until the district tells taxpayers the real maximum amount they’ll actually spend, Vote No on Prop H. Share this so more people know what’s really at stake. Listen to common sense Carl >>> https://www.youtube.com/live/gXJwYo-H72c... See less

items.author: Greenwood for FHSD School Board
items.bodyText: EXCITING NEWS — SAINT CHARLES COUNTY MOMS FOR LIBERTY CHAPTER IS RELAUNCHING! A few passionate parents originally started this chapter, but after seeing it wasn’t fully active and recognizing the real need that still exists in our community — especially as so many of you continue voicing the same concerns about parental rights, school transparency, and protecting our kids — I decided to step up and help bring it back stronger than ever! We’re relaunching with renewed energy and a low-commitment model — just ~8 meetings a year, $25 membership fee, and no pressure. This is about us coming together to support one another, lift each other up, and create real momentum for the changes our families need in ALL SCHOOL DISTRICTS across St. Charles County. Whether you’re ready to get involved or just want to connect with like-minded parents, you’re welcome here. Let’s stand together, encourage each other, and power one another forward! Join the Saint Charles County Chapter here: https://portal.momsforliberty.org/.../st-charles-county-mo/ #MomsForLiberty #StCharlesCounty #ParentalRights #FrancisHowell #WeAreStrongerTogether See less

Aristotle and Dante Discover the Secrets of the Universe by Benjamin Alire Sáenz Emotional Intensity 8/10 | Sexual Content 5/10 4. Someday, Someday, Maybe by Lauren Graham Drugs/Alcohol 6/10 | Sexual Content 5/10 5. Shine by Lauren Myracle Emotional Intensity 9/10 | Violence 8/10 6. The Passing Playbook by Isaac Fitzsimons (Gender transition, identity, discrimination, romantic content) 7. Two Boys Kissing by David Levithan Emotional Intensity 9/10 | Suicide/Mental Health 8/10 8. Simon vs. the Homo Sapiens Agenda by Becky Albertalli Sexual Content 5/10 | Language 5/10 9. Darius the Great Is Not Okay by Adib Khorram Suicide/Mental Health 8/10 | Emotional Intensity 8/10 10. Another Day by David Levithan Emotional Intensity 6/10 | Sexual Content 5/10 11. Neanderthal Opens the Door to the Universe by Preston Norton Language 9/10 | Suicide/Mental Health 8/10 12. Marco Impossible by Hannah Moskowitz Emotional Intensity 5/10 | Language 3/10 Request the full classroom library list from your child’s teacher or principal. Transparency shouldn’t be optional. items.bodyText: THIS 1:1 TECH POLICY SHOULDN’T BE HAPPENING TO OUR KIDS Francis Howell middle and high school students are required to take home district Chromebooks starting August 26 for FHN and carry them every single day. Extra weight in already heavy backpacks + more mandatory screen time is a direct hit on kids’ bodies and minds. Physical: Research consistently shows backpacks exceeding 10-15% of a student’s body weight increase neck, shoulder, and back pain plus postural problems. https://www.healthychildren.org/.../Backpack-Safety.aspx Emotional: Higher screen time is linked to increased anxiety and depression symptoms in adolescents. https://www.frontiersin.org/.../fpubh.2023.1101594/full Parents — push back. Email the Board of Education at board@fhsdschools.org and ask them to reconsider mandatory daily Chromebook carry and the added physical + emotional burden this places on students. See less

items.author: School Watchlist
items.bodyText: URGENT: School Board Members Celebrating Calls for Violence Against a Parent This is the level of “public education” leadership we are dealing with in Francis Howell. A post from the page “No to Francis Howell Families for FHSD” openly celebrated the idea that an entire group of women “would happily yeet Lauren out of the nearest window.” Yeet = to throw something (or someone) with force. In plain English: they are joking about throwing a parent out a window. That is a call for violence. That is wishing harm on a mother. And what did the newly elected do? • Sara Dillard (current FHSD School Board member) gave it a heart. Sara Dillard - Director, Francis Howell Board of Education https://www.facebook.com/share/19UkKS1T9T/?mibextid=wwXIfr • Ren Boehms Adams (wife of newly elected board member Jason Adams and Theater Director at FH Middle) jumped in and claimed the post as “that’s me!!” Jason Adams for FHSD @Ren Boehms Adams https://www.facebook.com/share/14owBPCEkqH/?mibextid=wwXIfr • Jen Bahr (wife of re-elected St. Charles Director of Elections @kurt Bahr) and recently elected Cottleville Township committee woman, and associated with their Bahr family properties real estate @Jen Bahr https://www.facebook.com/share/1EiDTqGJ21/?mibextid=wwXIfr Citizens for Kurt Bahr Multiple others piled on with likes. To every single person who liked or loved that comment — including Sara Dillard, Ren Boehms Adams and Jen Bahr: Do you support throwing a parent out a window? Are you in favor of a parent’s death or serious harm? If the answer is no, then why didn’t you condemn it? Why did you celebrate it instead? This is not “online banter.” This is elected officials and their spouses normalizing violent rhetoric against a mother who simply advocated for her children and other parents in this district. Francis Howell School District and Board: this must be stopped and dealt with immediately. This is a call to Publicly remove these people from their leadership positions, condemn this behavior and the board members and family members who celebrated it. Silence is approval. See less

items.bodyText: I’ll be voting YES on Amendment 4. Missouri’s Constitution isn’t just another law. It’s the foundation of how our state is governed, and I don’t believe it should be changed by a simple majority vote. The United States Constitution can’t be amended by a simple majority, and we don’t elect the President by a nationwide popular vote alone. We use the Electoral College because our system recognizes that different states and regions should have a voice, not just the largest population centers. Rural Missourians deserve a voice too! See less

items.author: Greenwood for FHSD School Board
items.bodyText: Putting Residents First As a Christian, wife, mother, and taxpayer, I understand the challenges facing St. Charles County families. As your County Council representative, I will fight for: • Eliminating the Personal Property Tax • Responsible Growth and Development • Improved Roads and Infrastructure • Election Integrity and Transparency • Accountable Government that Lives Within Its Means Our county is growing, but growth must be managed responsibly. We need to prioritize roads, public safety, schools, and infrastructure before approving more development. I believe the government should work for the people—not special interests. On August 4, I respectfully ask for your vote. Together, we can keep St. Charles County a great place to live, work, and raise a family. VOTE JUDI GAMBINO COUNTY COUNCIL DISTRICT 5 Common Sense • Accountability • Strong Families Thank you TheresaLPhoto for the beautiful photos. See less

items.bodyText: The U.S. House of Representatives has passed the "Stopping Indoctrination and Protecting Kids Act" (H.R. 2616), legislation aimed at restricting the use of federal education funds for teaching or promoting gender ideology in public elementary and middle schools. The bill would also require parental consent before schools make certain gender-related changes involving a child, including changes to names, pronouns, or access to sex-specific facilities. The bill must still pass the Senate and receive presidential approval before taking effect. Let's pray it does! #indoctrination #federal #education #funds #jesus #gender #Ideology #Senate #Trump #parents See less

items.bodyText: SHINY NEW TECH I feel this view oversimplifies the 1:1 Chromebook push at our schools and skips key details. Valid Concerns: 1. Device Shortfalls: They’re underestimating needs—ignoring breakage, theft, or loss. We’ll need way more than the initial estimate! 2. Tech Support Gap: No plans to add to the 25 Tech Aids or place them in schools. Teachers will end up as IT fixers, stealing time from teaching. 3. Unclear Usage: Just “strategic teaching” as the reason? No details on apps, integration, or curriculum fit. 4. Data Privacy Missing: Zero policies on protecting student info from third parties. Big red flag in today’s world! 5. Budget Blues: $1M per year for devices (totaling $5M over 5 years) + $2.3M for infrastructure (accounting for e-rate reimbursement, but they haven’t even received the last one requested). Both estimates are lowballs, and they ignore costs for increased staffing, infrastructure upgrades, device losses, blue light glasses to protect students’ eyes, or extra tech support. What about the fiscal cliff? 6. Internet Upgrades Needed: Current network probably won’t cut it—upgrades are essential, but are they fully planned? Bottom line: The pitch was all about buying/deploying, ignoring academic pros/cons. The current proposal covers only middle and high schools (not elementary). Feels like “keeping up with other districts” vibes from 2 years ago. Aside from all this info… what is the reason we are even looking to do this? Are there lots of students that don’t have access to a laptop at home? Wouldn’t it be more economical to only supply those in need? There is no way that just because the personal model is said to cost less than the classroom, that it’s going to cost less in total in the long run. It’s just not possible. This absolutely sets students up for more screen time. Have you seen the negative impacts on that? Back to the question: What problem are we trying to solve? Let’s discuss real student and taxpayer impacts! See less

items.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | I have heard some misconceptions from Thursday BOE Technology Update. We currently use a classroom approach to distribute chromebooks to high school and middle school students. This does require each classroom to have a higher number of chromebooks to match the hour with the largest class size. We are shifting to a personal chromebook model where each high school and middle school student will be assigned their own chromebook. Thursday’s Technology Update included these advantages to the change. 1- Money Savings - The personal chromebook model costs less than the classroom model. 2- Students can bring their personal chromebook home allowing for greater access to homework and Canva. 3- Students can more easily navigate the chromebook, as shared by Thursday’s student representative. This change in distribution does not mean students will be on technology more than before. It is simply a change in how chromebooks are assigned. This change provides greater efficiency for students and saves money for taxpayers. Win-Win. Transparency is only effective if it is connected to open, understandable communication. I hope this helps. Please feel free to ask questions. I’ll do my best to answer them. | kcdZzwZt.com
